sections.name: Compose reliable shell workflows
sections.outcome: Build and explain shell workflows that preserve data, combine commands, and automate repeated operations safely.
includes: shell expansion, quoting, variables, loops, conditionals, redirection, and pipelines
safe treatment of whitespace, newlines, glob characters, and command failures
excludes: system-wide network, identity, or storage policy

sample_tasks.instruction: Write a portable shell workflow that finds matching input files, derives one output name per input without corrupting spaces or punctuation, and stops if a conversion fails.
Diagnose a shell pipeline whose output changes when redirected to a file, then redesign the invocation so messages are captured in their intended order and destination.

sections.name: Inspect and preserve shell state
sections.outcome: Inspect and manipulate shell variables and expansion results without accidentally changing process state or losing embedded data.
includes: distinguishing shell variables from exported environment entries
quoting, parameter expansion, field splitting, and multiline values
excludes: parsing arbitrary command output when a structured interface is available

sample_tasks.instruction: In a POSIX shell, enumerate variables whose names share a prefix and print each complete value, including embedded newlines, without exporting or modifying the variables. Explain any portability limitation.
Explain why an unquoted expansion splits a stored filename into several words, and rewrite the surrounding loop so the original filename is preserved exactly.

sections.name: Transform files and text safely
sections.outcome: Select, rename, and transform files or text while preserving record boundaries and avoiding unintended matches or overwrites.
includes: filename decomposition and reconstruction
record filtering, substitution, sorting, aggregation, and null-delimited paths

sample_tasks.instruction: Given files such as ABC_1.fastq.Block12 and names that may contain spaces, produce the corresponding _2 names while preserving every other component and preventing collisions.
Design a pipeline that reports the ten most frequent status values from a large delimited log while rejecting malformed records rather than silently miscounting them.

sections.name: Control automated command execution
sections.outcome: Structure repeatable shell jobs with explicit sequencing, failure propagation, cleanup, and idempotent behavior.
includes: loops, conditionals, functions, exit status, traps, temporary resources, and scheduled execution
dry runs, reruns, concurrency bounds, and partial-failure handling
excludes: interactive one-command diagnosis with no reusable workflow

sample_tasks.instruction: Write a rerunnable shell job that processes every pending file once, records failures, cleans up temporary files on interruption, and returns a nonzero status if any item failed.

A nightly maintenance script continues after a failed database export and deletes yesterday's snapshot. Restructure its control flow so dependent steps run only after success and cleanup remains safe.

sections.name: Manage software and runtime configuration
sections.outcome: Discover, install, and configure software and process-wide runtime settings while accounting for scope, persistence, and dependency effects.
includes: package discovery, repository metadata, dependencies, and upgrades
environment, locale, timezone, search path, and runtime configuration scope
excludes: building and releasing software from source

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose an appropriate package for a requested capability, install it from configured repositories, and verify the executable and its dependencies without relying on a broad keyword match alone.
Change a host-wide runtime setting for all future sessions, apply the corresponding behavior immediately where possible, and explain which existing processes will not inherit the change.

sections.name: Select and maintain packaged software
sections.outcome: Resolve a software need to the correct package and perform installs, removals, or upgrades with understood repository and dependency consequences.
includes: exact package metadata, ownership lookup, dependencies, repository state, and version pinning
previewing and verifying package transactions

sample_tasks.instruction: A package search for git returns hundreds of descriptions. Narrow the result to the principal client and closely related official packages, using package metadata to justify the selection.
Before upgrading a shared command-line tool, determine the candidate version, packages that would be added or removed, and how to hold the current version if the preview is unsafe.

sections.name: Configure runtime context
sections.outcome: Set environment, locale, clock, and timezone behavior at the correct user, process, or host scope and verify when changes take effect.
includes: environment inheritance, startup files, locale, timezone data, clock synchronization, and process scope
distinguishing display conventions from the system clock
excludes: application-specific preference files unrelated to process runtime

sample_tasks.instruction: Change the system timezone for all users without rebooting, verify the active zone and clock synchronization state, and explain the effect on already running programs.
Configure a command to use a specific locale only for one invocation, then configure the same setting for one user's future login shells without affecting other users.

sections.name: Control and diagnose processes and services
sections.outcome: Operate processes and persistent services, tracing their execution, signals, streams, configuration, and logged failures to a defensible diagnosis.
includes: process lifecycle, signals, timers, standard streams, logs, service state, and daemon configuration
correlating observed behavior across process and service boundaries
excludes: application feature debugging unrelated to its operating environment

sample_tasks.instruction: A daemon repeatedly wakes earlier than its configured interval and writes messages to two destinations. Trace the responsible signals and streams, then specify a robust operational correction.
A newly configured directory proxy starts but returns only part of the expected directory. Distinguish lifecycle, binding, routing, and access-control causes using service state and logs.

sections.name: Coordinate process lifecycle and timing
sections.outcome: Start, stop, wait for, signal, and schedule processes without races, orphaned work, or incorrect timing assumptions.
includes: process trees, jobs, exit status, signal delivery, interrupted waits, timers, and graceful termination
distinguishing process-wide and thread-specific effects

sample_tasks.instruction: Explain why a thread's 60-second sleep repeatedly ends after another thread's timer signal, and revise the timing logic so it waits until the intended deadline.
Design a shutdown sequence for a parent process and several workers that stops accepting work, gives active tasks a deadline, and escalates termination without leaving children behind.

sections.name: Trace output streams and logs
sections.outcome: Determine where process output went and reconstruct event order despite separate streams, buffering, redirection, and concurrent writers.
includes: standard input, output, and error; descriptor duplication; buffering; log filtering and rotation
timestamps and process identity for correlating events
excludes: general text transformation without an operational diagnosis
application correctness inferred solely from message order

sample_tasks.instruction: A program prints some messages to the terminal and others to a redirected file, with the apparent order changing under nohup. Identify the stream and buffering causes and give capture options with clear ordering limits.

Investigate a service restart by extracting the relevant time window from its logs, separating messages from old and new process instances, and identifying the first causal error rather than later symptoms.

sections.name: Configure and operate persistent services
sections.outcome: Translate a service topology into valid configuration, apply changes safely, and verify behavior from both service and client perspectives.
includes: configuration validation, dependencies, startup policy, reload versus restart, health checks, and failover
proxies and replicated backends when diagnosing request routing
excludes: host route selection independent of a service

sample_tasks.instruction: Configure a read-only proxy for two replicated directory backends that serve the same naming context, validate the configuration, and define client checks for failover and complete search results.
Roll out a daemon configuration change with syntax validation, a reload when supported, health verification, and an explicit rollback point if clients begin failing.

sections.name: Configure network reachability and access
sections.outcome: Establish intended connectivity and authorization by reasoning about route choice, name resolution, identities, permissions, and authentication boundaries.
includes: interfaces, routes, gateways, metrics, policy rules, DNS, users, groups, modes, ACLs, and credentials
verification from the affected user or client context
excludes: application authorization rules that do not rely on host or directory identities

sample_tasks.instruction: Configure a multi-interface host so private destinations use the organization link, general traffic prefers a mobile link with fallback, and joining a trusted wireless network supersedes both policies.
Grant a service account read access to one protected directory tree without exposing it to other users, then verify both the allowed and denied cases.

sections.name: Select and verify network paths
sections.outcome: Predict and configure the path traffic takes across interfaces and gateways, including preference changes and failure behavior.
includes: longest-prefix matching, default routes, metrics, policy routing, interface state, and DNS reachability
source-address and return-path considerations
excludes: service-layer load balancing among healthy application instances

sample_tasks.instruction: Given three active interfaces and their subnets, propose routes and priorities that keep 10.0.0.0/8 on Ethernet, prefer cellular for other traffic, fall back to Ethernet, and override both when Wi-Fi connects.
A host can reach an external address but replies to inbound connections leave through the wrong gateway. Trace the selected forward and return paths and correct the relevant routing policy.

sections.name: Administer identities and permissions
sections.outcome: Assign least-privilege access through users, groups, ownership, permissions, and authentication policy, then test the effective result.
includes: account lifecycle, groups, ownership, mode bits, ACLs, privilege delegation, secrets, and directory access rules
effective identity and inherited or default permissions
excludes: application roles that are wholly internal to an application

sample_tasks.instruction: Create a shared project directory where members of one group can create and edit files, new entries inherit the group, and unrelated users cannot read the contents. Verify the effective access.
Allow an operator to run one administrative maintenance command without a general privileged shell, while preserving auditability and preventing argument-based privilege expansion.

sections.name: Maintain storage and recoverability
sections.outcome: Manage filesystem capacity and persistence while creating and validating recoverable copies of system and application data.
includes: filesystems, mounts, devices, capacity, archives, snapshots, backups, retention, restore, and integrity checks
safe operational sequencing around live data
excludes: remote service replication treated as a substitute for backup

sample_tasks.instruction: A host is nearly out of space while a critical service is writing data. Identify the responsible filesystem and growth source, reclaim or extend capacity safely, and confirm the service remains consistent.
Design and test a recovery procedure for a service whose configuration and mutable data require different backup schedules and consistency handling.

sections.name: Operate filesystems and storage capacity
sections.outcome: Inspect, mount, resize, and repair storage while protecting data and accounting for device, filesystem, and open-file behavior.
includes: block devices, partitioning, filesystems, mounts, inode and byte usage, quotas, and safe unmounting
diagnosing deleted-but-open files and persistent mount configuration
excludes: database-level logical consistency beyond quiescing requirements

sample_tasks.instruction: Disk usage remains full after a large log is deleted. Determine whether an open file, inode exhaustion, or a hidden mount explains the discrepancy and remediate without rebooting.
Add a new volume for application data, create an appropriate filesystem, mount it persistently by stable identity, and verify ownership and behavior after a mount-cycle test.

sections.name: Create and validate recoverable backups
sections.outcome: Choose backup and snapshot procedures that meet recovery goals, preserve required metadata, and prove restoration through testing.
includes: full and incremental copies, snapshots, consistency, retention, encryption, integrity, and restore drills
recovery point and recovery time tradeoffs
excludes: copying files without a stated retention or recovery contract

sample_tasks.instruction: Plan backups for a changing dataset with a four-hour recovery-point target and limited repository capacity, including retention, consistency, integrity checks, and a restore drill.
Restore one accidentally deleted directory from an encrypted backup into a staging location, verify contents and metadata, and return it to service without overwriting newer unrelated data.
